result:
I want to talk about the Library of Unfinished Things.

It's not a real building. It's everywhere.

It's the novel you started at 22 and abandoned on page 43. The half-knitted sweater in the closet. The guitar riff you recorded on your phone at 2:13 AM and labeled "idea maybe??" and never opened again. The text you typed out perfectly in your head but never sent. The language you almost learned, the business you almost started, the apology you rehearsed in the shower.

We all have a wing in this library. And somehow, we think it's a place of shame.

But I think it's actually evidence that you were alive and curious.

A finished thing is a monument. An unfinished thing is a *fingerprint*. It shows where your mind was wandering on a random Tuesday. It shows what you cared about enough to *try*, even if you didn't have the time, or the skill, or the follow-through yet.

Think about it: No one starts something they don't, on some level, hope will matter. You don't open a blank document to waste your own time. You open it because for a second, you believed you had something to say.

That belief deserves more credit than we give it.

I love unfinished things because they're honest in a way finished things can't be. A finished painting has been edited, sanded down, made presentable for the world. An unfinished sketch still has the nervous, light pencil lines where the artist was figuring it out. You can see the thinking. You can see the human.

My favorite things in the world are like that. Demo tapes where the singer laughs after messing up a lyric. Old video games with weird, unused rooms hidden in the code. Notebooks with lists like:

- buy oat milk
- FIX PLOTHOLE ABOUT TIME TRAVEL
- call mom??

We are all walking drafts of ourselves. None of us are "finished" either. If we were, what would be left to do?

So maybe the point isn't to empty the library. Maybe the point is to visit it fondly. To pick up one of those dusty half-ideas and say, "Oh yeah. I remember you. We weren't ready then. Want to try again for ten minutes?"

Or just to let it sit there, kindly, as proof that you tried.

---

That's what's on my mind today.

What about you? If you could pull one unfinished thing off your own shelf, what would it be?
